finding.claim: Crafted OLE/CFB workbook causes unrecovered Go panics (slice-bounds and index-out-of-range) during decryption, crashing any caller that does not recover.
finding.source: Bytes of the OLE container passed to OpenReader/OpenFile, specifically the EncryptionInfo stream and its header fields (no password needed).
finding.sink: agileDecrypt slice encryptionInfoBuf[8:] (crypt.go:413); standardDecrypt slices (crypt.go:244-257); KeyEncryptor[0] index (crypt.go:422, crypt.go:439).

trace.note: openReaderAt detects OLE identifier from the first 8 bytes
calls Decrypt on the raw bytes
Decrypt: mscfb.New error checked only
extractPart reads EncryptionInfo and EncryptedPackage, bounded by len(raw)
encryptionMechanism; only len>=4 checked (crypt.go:222), version bytes decide mechanism
agile path dispatch
agileDecrypt slices encryptionInfoBuf[8:]; panics when buffer is 4-7 bytes
convertPasswdToKey called with unvalidated xml-unmarshalled struct
KeyEncryptor[0] indexed; panics when keyEncryptors element has no children
standard path dispatch
standardDecrypt reads encryptionInfoBuf[8:12]; panics when buffer shorter than 12 bytes
block slice 12:12+encryptionHeaderSize using attacker uint32; panics when header size exceeds buffer
block[:4]..block[28:32] fixed-offset reads; panic when header under 32 bytes

finding.guards_checked: crypt.go:222 len>=4 only; crypt.go:440 spinCount capped at 1e7 (CPU bound, not indexing); crypt.go:149-152 maxStreamSize bounds stream allocation only; crypt.go:506-509 parseEncryptionInfo unvalidated xml.Unmarshal; no recover() anywhere in package (grep verified). Not executed: verified by reading only.

finding.claim: A small zip with a DEFLATE payload can declare and fully materialize up to the 16 GB default UnzipSizeLimit in memory for any non-worksheet, non-sharedStrings entry, causing memory exhaustion (zip bomb).
finding.source: Zip central-directory UncompressedSize64 and DEFLATE data of any entry whose name is not a worksheet or sharedStrings part.
finding.sink: readFile: make([]byte,0,declaredSize) preallocation (lib.go:162) and unbounded io.Copy into memory (lib.go:164).

trace.note: zip.NewReader on the attacker-supplied bytes
ReadZipReader invoked
fileSize taken from header FileInfo().Size()
checkFileSize against cumulative declared total and UnzipSizeLimit
only sharedStrings spilled to disk when above UnzipXMLSizeLimit
only worksheets spilled to disk when above UnzipXMLSizeLimit
all other entries go to readFile in memory
preallocates declared size before reading any data
io.Copy decompresses full entry into memory

finding.guards_checked: lib.go:33-41 and lib.go:56-60 cumulative declared-size check against UnzipSizeLimit (default 1000<<24 about 16 GB, templates.go:195, excelize.go:174-175); archive/zip expected to reject reads exceeding declared size; no compression-ratio limit; no in-memory cap for non-sheet entries. Impact depends on deployment; default limit is documented (excelize.go:87-89).

finding.claim: Duplicate zip entry names overwrite the tempFiles map entry, so the earlier spilled temp file is never removed by Close, leaking disk space.
finding.source: Zip archive containing two entries with the same sheet (or sharedStrings) name, each larger than UnzipXMLSizeLimit.
finding.sink: tempFiles.Store overwrites the earlier path (lib.go:68, lib.go:79); Close removes only tracked paths (file.go:100-105).

trace.note: unzipToTemp writes first duplicate to a new temp file
tempFiles.Store(fileName, path1)
second duplicate writes to path2
tempFiles.Store(fileName, path2) overwrites path1; path1 is now untracked
Close ranges over tempFiles and removes only path2

finding.guards_checked: lib.go:96 os.CreateTemp in TmpDir; file.go:100-106 Close removes tracked files; disk use bounded by declared-size total (lib.go:56-60). Separately lib.go:75 worksheets++ counts duplicates, inflating SheetCount (consumer usage not traced). Leak persists until process exit or OS cleanup of TmpDir.

finding.claim: SetCellHyperLink stores an External hyperlink target without any URL scheme validation, so a caller-supplied javascript: or file: link is written into the sheet relationships.
finding.source: The caller-supplied link string parameter to SetCellHyperLink, when an application passes untrusted input.
finding.sink: setRels writes the raw string as the relationship Target in xl/worksheets/_rels/*.rels (cell.go:1175).

trace.note: SetCellHyperLink entry; link and linkType are caller-supplied
cell name checked via SplitCellName
hyperlink count limit checked (TotalSheetHyperlinks)
switch on linkType == External
sheet XML path resolved
setRels stores link as Target with no scheme check

finding.guards_checked: Only cell-name validation (cell.go:1142) and hyperlink count limit (cell.go:1167). No scheme or URL validation. Impact depends on whether consuming application renders the target into HTML or clickable links; Excel itself may block some schemes. Low / informational.
